title: Tiered latency envelope and automated fallback playbook
creator: Asha Patel
description: PRD-level ticket to define a multi-tier latency envelope and the automated fallback/playbook that will be used during progressive rollouts. Scope covers: defining per-workload latency envelopes (p50/p90/p95) for interactive chat, embeddings, and batch generation; specifying error-budget burn-rate thresholds and subsequent automated actions (throttle, model-fallback, regional-shift); rollout gates and acceptance criteria for canary and gradual ramp; and integration points with Console observability (dashboards/alerts) and Redwood Optimize recommendations. This is a product-first specification (not implementation) and will drive engineering stories for runtime, routing, and Console changes. Scope changes/clarifications since kickoff: added explicit per-tenant soft-SLOs to support priority tiers; included cost-savings target for model fallback paths; require synthetic-load and chaos tests as part of acceptance.
acceptance_criteria: Define latency envelopes for three workload classes: interactive-chat (target p50 <= 120ms, p90 <= 300ms, p95 <= 420ms), embeddings (p50 <= 60ms, p90 <= 180ms), and bulk-generation (p50 <= 300ms, p90 <= 900ms)

Document a prioritized model-fallback chain for each workload and region (primary -> quantized variant -> distilled/cheaper model) including compatibility table and expected degradation in semantic quality

Specify automated gates: (a) Canary pause if canary burn-rate > 2x baseline error budget for 10m; (b) Automatic rollback if p95 latency or error-rate exceeds gate threshold for 3 consecutive 5m windows

Error budget policy: define daily and weekly burn-rate thresholds and exact mitigation actions at each tier (throttle at 2x, regional-shift at 4x, model-fallback at 6x) and describe alerting escalation path
Provide concrete test plans: load test runbook that demonstrates model-fallback triggers under controlled traffic and verifies clients see fallback with <10s user-visible interruption in 95% of cases
Console integration: dashboard mockups and alert rules exist and a CI job emits synthetic SLO signals to validate alerting end-to-end
Per-tenant soft-SLOs documented with example policy for high-priority customers including override and manual intervention steps
Cost target: fallback path should reduce per-token infra cost by at least 25% relative to primary model for equivalent throughput within 95% of test runs
Security/Compliance: no customer data is routed outside requested region during automated fallbacks unless explicit tenant opt-in is documented

implementation_notes: Engineering will need runtime changes: rollout guard hooks, automated model-switch API, and per-tenant policy evaluation in router layer
Console changes: SLO dashboard panels, machine-readable canary rules, and on-call playbook link in alert emails
Testing: include a staged load-test job in CI that can inject synthetic errors and simulate region outage; coordinate with SRE for chaos experiments
Data collection: ensure token-level latency traces and model-version tags are emitted to the tracing pipeline for rollback diagnostics
risks: Automated fallback may increase load on cheaper models leading to cascading latency regressions if not capacity-aware
Per-tenant overrides add operational complexity and possible divergence between Console and runtime enforcement
Quality regression risk when switching to distilled models — need guardrail evaluation and automatic rollback based on semantic quality metrics
